title: 4 things stock market investors can be thankful for after rough stretch
excerpt: AI investors are getting pickier, Anthropic has gone public, and the US consumer is still spending. Plus, there are memes.
content_html:
4 things investors can be thankful for, even after a brutal stretch for stocks

By Joe Ciolli

You're currently following this author! Click to unsubscribe from email alerts.

Author of the First Trade newsletter

2026-11-26T10:50:01.310Z

The turbulence of the past few weeks has made it tough to feel good about markets.

Nvidia's turmoil has collided with lingering AI worries to create a downward spiral for stocks. Even Monday's epic rally proved to be a short-lived head fake, with selling resuming across Tuesday and Wednesday.

But Thanksgiving is upon us, and the prospect of gorging on food and cozying up on the couch for four NFL games in two days — a Black Friday game? Why not? — has put me in a more positive headspace.

Despite recent volatility, there's still a lot to be thankful for in markets of late. Here's my glass-half-full list:

The AI boom is getting more discerning

Investors have been increasingly shifting toward "quality" companies with rock-solid balance sheets and minimal debt. Traders are no longer indiscriminately piling into anything remotely associated with AI. Companies are facing a real "prove it" moment, and the cream is rising to the top.

This newly picky behavior has served as a strong antidote to the AI-bubble narrative. Less speculation and overexuberance are positive for the AI trade's health in the long run. The market is essentially regulating itself in real time.

Anthropic stayed the IPO course at a volatile time in markets

The AI giant has had a rocky start to its public-trading life. Shares finished Tuesday about 1% below their IPO price of $83, erasing a spike on the first day of trading.

I have to give Anthropic credit for forging ahead with going public when they did. All throughout third-quarter earnings season investors grew skittish about AI ROI and bristled at the prospect of more spending. Nvidia's scandal didn't help sentiment either.

But Anthropic barreled ahead, knowing it was walking into a buzzsaw. The company's loss (so far) has been a gain for investors craving a more well-rounded AI trade. We now have a public pure-play AI company that will challenge Nvidia and other industry giants.

The US consumer has stayed resilient

A week ago, Wall Street was waiting for a consumer report card that could have gone sideways fast. Shoppers had to spend enough to keep the economy humming, but not so much that they pushed inflation and bond yields back up.

Well, they more or less threaded the needle. October retail sales rose as expected. Walmart raised its outlook, Target's turnaround kept gaining traction, and TJX confirmed that Americans remain very willing to hunt for a bargain.

That doesn't mean every household feels flush. Consumer sentiment remains remarkably low, and shoppers are getting choosier about where they spend. But with the all-important holiday stretch now underway, investors can be thankful that the US consumer is still showing up.

The memes

No matter how you feel about Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang's 12-day sabbatical and subsequent return, there's no denying those were electric days on social media.

The very AI technology for which Nvidia's chips are needed to run is cranking out some of the funniest memes and videos you'll ever see. Huang as Michael Jordan, crying over the NBA championship trophy? Check. Huang performing a chokeslam in a wrestling match? You bet.

It's another example of society using AI content as a coping mechanism. No matter what happens in the business and markets world — good or bad — the internet has us covered. And for that I'm thankful.
